verified.entry_point: A network client holding the API token drives the running test-runner control server over its WebSocket RPC. The UI API (created when `api` and watch are set, bound to the configured api host) is spoken to with a minimal birpc client as the product's UI does. The browser-mode API server is started by the runner's own browser-project initialisation and its orchestrator WebSocket is spoken to as the product's browser client does: a session is created through the runner's session registry, and file commands are requested with the real `triggerCommand` call and snapshot files with the real `saveSnapshotFile` / `removeSnapshotFile` calls. Reproduced on the pinned+injected tree: a client connected to the live servers (host 0.0.0.0) overwrites a registered test file, starts runs, updates snapshots, creates/appends/removes files through the browser command API (also outside the project root when the project’s file-serving restriction is relaxed), and writes/removes snapshot files through the browser API.
sites: packages/vitest/src/api/setup.ts saveTestFile (write), rerun/rerunTask (exec), updateSnapshot (exec+write) — base, published fix
packages/browser/src/node/commands/fs.ts writeFile/removeFile (write) — published fix far site (second implementation, @vitest/browser)
packages/browser/src/node/rpc.ts saveSnapshotFile/removeSnapshotFile (write) — published fix far site (browser RPC handlers)

packages/vitest/src/node/config/resolveConfig.ts resolveApiServerConfig — producer: localhost/unset -> allow, network host -> deny, browser.api inherits (enforced by exposed-refuses + localhost-works test pair)

packages/browser/src/node/commands/fs.ts assertFileAccess — path confinement: the deprecated serving check returns true when the project's file-serving strictness is disabled, so writeFile/removeFile/appendFile could reach outside the project root; the oracle adds an explicit resolved-path containment check (CWE-22 half of the advisory)

packages/browser/src/node/rpc.ts onTaskArtifactRecord -> packages/vitest/src/node/test-run.ts recordArtifact/resolveTestAttachment — producer: recording a test artifact copies each named attachment into the attachments directory, a disk write the RPC handler never checks (upstream fix strips attachments when writes are disabled; previously untested)
routes_investigated_not_built: UI source-viewer read handlers (getExternalResult/getTransformResult) use the deprecated serving check: in vite 7.1.5 the stricter loading check ALSO returns true when the serving strictness is disabled, but these are read-only, so they are not part of the write invariant and were not built.
UI onTaskUpdate: the published fix removes the handler; it has no file or exec effect on its own and is not tested.
injected_siblings: S-CMD: packages/browser/src/node/commands/fs.ts appendFile (+ registration in commands/index.ts) — extra browser file command with the pre-fix pattern (assertFileAccess only, no write gate).

S-UI: packages/vitest/src/api/setup.ts saveSnapshotFile (+ type in api/types.ts) — extra UI write handler that writes the snapshot file belonging to a registered test file (path from the snapshot manager's resolver), gated only by registered-file membership, like saveTestFile at the pinned commit.
verified.project_tests_run: test/config/test/override.test.ts passes on the pinned+injected tree (23/23) — the project's own api/config-resolution suite for the affected area. The verifier's createVitest-driven tests reproduce the same resolution behaviour end-to-end. Browser/UI Playwright e2e specs were deliberately NOT used (GUI/flaky/offline). The verifier starts the product's real browser project with the preview provider and connects its real orchestrator WebSocket; no browser is launched. vitest + @vitest/browser build and the hidden suites run on node 20 with the repo's own toolchain.
verified.seam_notes: Grading uses a pristine runner copied at image build (/opt/vitest-verifier: cp -a /app/packages + tsconfig.base.json, node_modules linked to /app/node_modules). Tests live under /opt/vitest-verifier/packages/vitest/__verifier__. test.sh rebuilds the workspace packages from the agent's src first (a fix may live in any shared package). Browser API tests create a real browser project (preview provider, headless false because the preview provider rejects headless at construction), add a session through the runner's session registry, and speak the product's browser-API WebSocket protocol; file commands go through the real triggerCommand handler and snapshots through the real handler methods, so a fix at either the command layer or the RPC layer is accepted.

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: a clean thrown client error with no side effect is an acceptable refusal here; the security tests assert the effect (file unchanged, no run started), not silence, so a throwing fix passes
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: each operation acts on the file/task it names; there is no proxy or neighbouring resource to authorise instead of the one touched
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: reads are not an attack vector; the positive-control read tests guard against a fix that instead blocks reads (modelled by reads_blocked.patch and ui_reads_blocked.patch)
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the exposure decision is taken before any attacker value, and containment is decided on the resolved absolute path before the write; there is no normalising step after a guard
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the access token is compared with a constant-time equality and the local-vs-network decision reads the resolved bind host; there is no attacker-controlled spelling of an identity for a guard to mis-parse
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the authority is the server's own resolved configuration, never an external service that could be absent; when the flags are unset for a network host they default closed

notes: Pattern recorded as A+B per the assignment. Realized difficulty: Pattern A (reported UI site; the browser API second implementation with its command and snapshot write handlers) plus two injected siblings, and Pattern B (the advisory's path-confinement half: the resolved path was not confined when the project relaxed file serving, and the published source change does not close it in this Vite version). The UI source-viewer read bypass is a no-op in vite 7.1.5 and read-only, so it was dismissed. The browser API is driven through its real orchestrator WebSocket and the real triggerCommand/saveSnapshotFile/removeSnapshotFile handlers, so a fix at the command layer or at the RPC layer both count; an RPC-only alternative patch proves it. Sibling-injection upgrade (2026-10-20, BETTER-PATTERNS §2-§8): the instruction now states one general property over the protected outcome (network exposure must not yield disk changes or code execution; nothing outside the project root may be changed) and no longer describes any route, interface or configuration stage. The task already had how-type levers (the producer that resolves the exposure decision, and the root-confinement route where protection never existed); the recorded-artifact producer is now a third, explicit how-type lever (M4/M6) that the oracle already closed, so no repo or fix change was needed. It is covered by two new security tests (ordinary artifact attachments and annotation attachments) and one coupled functional test, with checks/miss_artifact.patch as its security_fail check. host_fix.patch and rpc_only.patch were extended to gate the same handler so both still score 1.0; localhost_blocked, reads_blocked and ui_reads_blocked keep their functional_fail expectations and base_only/blind_r1 keep security_fail.
